decision_reason: NASA's software catalog identifies NTRT v1 as an open-source C++/MATLAB toolkit for modeling, simulating, and controlling tensegrity robots and links to this exact public simulator repository. NASA TechPort identifies NASA Ames as the lead organization for a project integrating NTRT with Pleiades, while NASA's 2014 NTRS paper documents NTRT's validation against hardware. The repository has an exact Apache-2.0 grant; its first LICENSE commit is dated 2014-06-05, when code was already present. It includes detailed build/install guidance, and a substantive 2026 refresh updates source/setup for Apple Silicon. This is the toolkit simulator/product family, not each example or downstream research model as a separate product.

government_provenance.note: NASA's exact NTRT v1 product record describes the toolkit and links Download Now to the reviewed repository. NASA TechPort's project 146071 names NTRT and lists Ames Research Center as lead for integration with Pleiades: https://techport.nasa.gov/projects/146071.

public_source.note: The public canonical repository exposes C++/MATLAB simulator source, tests, examples, INSTALL instructions, and documentation without credentials.

eligible_license.note: The repository root contains the full Apache License 2.0 grant, an OSI-approved license, for this project's source. Third-party dependencies remain under their own licenses.

primary_evidence.note: NASA catalogs NTRT v1 as a reusable open-source software product; INSTALL supplies build/setup guidance. The 2014 NASA NTRS paper names the NASA Ames Dynamic Tensegrity Robotics Lab's software environments and reports simulator validation against hardware (https://ntrs.nasa.gov/citations/20140010928). Repository history shows a substantive 2026-06-16 macOS/Apple Silicon refresh.

decision_reason: The assigned canonical repository is a Medicaid Provider Enrollment Screening Portal challenge-code project created through NASA CoECI's interagency work with CMS, not the source record's claimed CoECI-CMS-Open-Payment. The source record URL https://github.com/nasa/CoECI-CMS-Open-Payment returns 404; the accessible NASA-Tournament-Lab repository is specifically MPSP. Its README contains an Apache-2.0 licensing notice for the TopCoder-authored project code and describes the 2012–2013 challenge, but no current exact-code deployment/support or versioned release was verified. Hold this exact URL pending a current product/code-parity signal and clarification of the metadata mismatch; do not relabel it as Open Payment.

decision_reason: The repository contains the top five submissions from USAID/Humanity United's Tech Challenge for Atrocity Prevention, rather than an agency-developed, versioned, reusable software product. Although it exposes C++/Java competition source and an Apache-2.0 LICENSE, the README says users must retrieve a separate input-data archive (including a placeholder URL) and read the contest problem statement to understand the individual solutions. No independent reuse, operational product, versioned release, or current product-specific support was established. Reject this challenge-submission bundle as a standalone catalog product.

government_provenance.note: The FY2013 federal prize-authority report says USAID, with Humanity United, implemented the Tech Challenge for Atrocity Prevention and worked with NASA CoECI on four competitions; the repo README identifies this exact bundle as solutions from that challenge.

public_source.note: The public repository contains the competition's C++/Java solution files and README without credentials.

eligible_license.note: The actual root LICENSE is the standard Apache License 2.0, an OSI-approved grant, for the repository's submissions.

primary_evidence.note: The README identifies a package of the top five competition submissions, says users need the external contest problem statement and dataset to run them, and provides no independently versioned release or user product documentation. The data-download placeholder and competition-specific solutions show this is a challenge artifact, not a demonstrated reusable government product.

decision_reason: This is an exact NASA-released research-code artifact for the peer-reviewed 2021 plasma space-time reconstruction paper. NASA's code catalog currently lists the exact repository and use, and the exact NASA Open Source Agreement v1.3 is OSI-approved for the designated software. However, this repo also bundles simulation datasets and trained model weights while the agreement defines its covered subject as software/source/object code and accompanying documentation; no separate data/weights grant was found. Hold pending clarification or a separately scoped license for those bundled research artifacts, rather than treating the code grant as automatically covering them.

government_provenance.note: The actual agreement identifies NASA as Government Agency, GSC-18879-1 as designation, and 'Transformer Neural Network for 1D MHD reconstruction' as the original software title. The peer-reviewed paper identifies authors in NASA Goddard Space Flight Center's Geospace Physics Lab and NASA funding.

public_source.note: The repository publicly exposes Python source, notebooks, README, simulation HDF5 data, model weights, and license without credentials.

eligible_license.note: The software license is NASA Open Source Agreement v1.3 (NASA-1.3), OSI-approved (https://opensource.org/license/NASA-1.3), and is explicitly scoped to the designated software/source and accompanying documentation. The repository also includes generated simulation data and model weights, whose treatment under this software grant or separate terms is not stated; this review does not assume those artifacts are licensed by the code grant.

primary_evidence.note: NASA's exact code.nasa.gov listing describes this repository as the code used in the identified 2021 paper for one-dimensional MHD shock-tube reconstruction and states that it includes source, data, and notebooks for scientific reproduction. That listing says last updated July 1, 2026. The peer-reviewed paper reports the exact reconstruction experiments and funding (https://www.frontiersin.org/journals/astronomy-and-space-sciences/articles/10.3389/fspas.2021.732275/full).
